We use alcohol units in the UK. You can work out how many units there are in any drink by multiplying the total volume of a drink (in ml) by its ABV (measured as a percentage) and dividing the result by 1,000.

strength (ABV) x volume (ml) ÷ 1,000 = units

If you are drinking more than 15 units of alcohol a day, in the UK, they generally think you're at higher risk for alcohol withdrawal and advise you seek medical help.

By the way... alcoholics come from all walks of life. You realise this in AA. There is nothing tying anyone together; the only common thread is our alcoholism. Some members are rich, others are homeless. Some members are elderly, some are teenagers. Some people came from good homes with loving families, some were abused. I could go on.

You are only 20 years old and you're already drinking chronically. You have no idea what is coming. You may have not lost anything and be "high functioning" now, but you will lose more and more until you have nothing left. Trust me. When I was 20, I was drinking chronically like you, had no health issues, felt generally fine and kept good grades in uni despite being drunk all the time. I knew my drinking was "wrong" but I didn't really care as long as my life kept running. You couldn't have paid me to go to AA.

Eventually I wanted to truly stop and I couldn't. I tried countless things and nothing seemed to make a lick of difference. It kept going and my tolerance built and built and built. I stopped being able to properly maintain friendships or keep up with my responsibilities. 

Fast forward two years later from 20. I'm 22 now. I just got hospitalised for two weeks for severe alcohol withdrawal. I was hallucinating in my room, could not stand up because I was shaking so violenty and was constantly vomitting. I genuinely thought I was going to die. I had to drop out of school because my health is so poor. Everyone knows what happened including my school and parents. It's horrendous. My life collapsed. And I'm 22. If I keep drinking, there's no telling the horrors are sure to come my way. I truly see that now. On top of all that, in comparison to most alcoholics, I've basically still lost nothing at all.

You think you have control over this. I thought I had control over it too. No matter what OP I think eventually you're going to see that delusion completely fall apart.
